description: A 2D label placement library for engineering drawings that automatically arranges labels to prevent overlaps with each other and blocked regions. Features 5 layout algorithms: Greedy, Bounded Backtracking, Simulated Annealing, Force-Directed, and Constraint Satisfaction.
releaseNotes:
BREAKING CHANGES
      - GeoPolyline is now always an open chain. The IsClosed property is removed, along with the
        constructor overloads that took a closed flag. Geometry that encloses an area is a GeoPolygon;
        call polyline.ToPolygon() to convert.
      - Containment.Contains(GeoPolyline, GeoPoint) is removed. A curve has no interior, so the check
        only ever restated Containment.IsPointOn, which is what to call instead. This also brings
        GeoPolyline in line with GeoLine, which never had a Contains overload.
      - A polyline no longer reports an enclosed region anywhere: Containment.Locate returns OnSide or
        OutSide only, Distance.DistanceTo measures to the path rather than returning zero for interior
        points, and Collision no longer treats a traced loop as containing the shapes inside it.
      - Parametrization now clamps polyline parameters and distances to the endpoints instead of
        wrapping them. Wrapping remains the behaviour of the closed curves: GeoPolygon, GeoRectangle
        and GeoCircle.

      NEW
      - Splition: splits a GeoLine or GeoPolyline at a point, at an arc length, or where a cutting line
        crosses it. Pieces are returned in order along the subject. Cut positions outside the subject or
        on its endpoints are skipped, positions closer together than the tolerance are merged, and a
        position near an existing vertex snaps onto it, so no piece and no edge is shorter than the
        tolerance.
      - Splition: splits a GeoLine or GeoPolyline at a point, at an arc length, or wherever a cutter
        meets it. Cutters may be a line, a polyline, a polygon, or an array of any of those, and several
        polygons behave as their union. Splitting against a polygon sorts the result by side; a polyline
        subject keeps each run whole as a GeoPolyline rather than breaking it into segments. A part
        running along the boundary counts as inside, and a path that touches the boundary and turns back
        is not a crossing.
      - Every split overload leaves its out parameters usable when it returns false: an array form hands
        back the subject as a single piece rather than a null array.
      - A point that does not lie on the subject is refused by every overload that takes points, the
        array forms included, instead of being projected onto the subject and cut at.
      - Every split is also reachable as an instance method on the shape being cut: GeoLine and
        GeoPolyline now carry TrySplitBy, TrySplitAtDistance, SplitAtDistances and SplitBy, matching how
        the other Operations classes are mirrored. They sit on the subject rather than the cutter, since
        polygon.Split(line) would not say which of the two comes back in pieces.
      - GeoPoint.IsPointOn(GeoLine), closing a gap where a point could be tested against a polyline and
        a circle but not against a line segment.

      FIXES
      - Splitting results are built through an internal constructor that skips revalidation, so an
        explicit tolerance passed by the caller is no longer overridden by Tolerance.Global.
      - README documented an IntersectsWith method family that does not exist; the correct names are
        CollidesWith and GetIntersections. Every README snippet is now covered by a unit test.
